findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing. Education was provided. Ensure that employees washing their hands properly before donning gloves at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The nozzles of the fountain drink machine are observed soiled with a dark brown/ black slimy substance. PIC is instructed to clean the food contact surfaces often enough to prevent build up. The nozzles were cleaned and rand through the dish during the inspection to correct. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing. The following areas of the facility are in need of cleaning: 1) The floors under the shelves in the walk in cooler are heavily soiled with food debris. 2) The shelf above the hand sink in the kitchen area is soiled with dust. 3) The held in the middle of the kitchen over the single service items is soiled with dust. 4) The hood system over the stove is soiled with dust. The PIC is instructed to clean the facility often enough to prevent accumulation of dust/ food debris.
5) 6-201.11  (C) The hand sink in the kitchen is observed pulling away from the wall and to have a crack that is not smooth and easily clean able. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily clean able. PIC is instructed to repair (recaulk) the sink to wall gap to facilitate a smooth easily clean able surface.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the shelving throughout the kitchen to have dust accumulation (and some grease accumulation) on them. Clean the shelving units as often as necessary to prevent soil and dust accumulation. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment: 1) Observed the lights throughout the kitchen and dry storage areas to be unshielded. Shields were reported to have been taken off to repaint the ceiling and need to be reinstalled. 2) Observed the ventilation hood baffles over the stovetop/fryer area to have dust and grease accumulation. Clean the ventilation hood baffles. 6-202.11  (C) Lighting was found not shielded. Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Reference 6-202.11.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.12  (C) Make-up air / Exhaust vents were found with accumulation of dust on them. Heating, ventilating, and air conditioning systems shall be designed and installed so that make-up air intake and exhaust vents do not cause contamination of food, food-contact surfaces, equipment, or utensils. Reference 6-202.12.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed ham dated 1/15 and sausages and sauce without date marking in the walk in cooler. Ham was discarded, and sausages and sauce were date marked with their reported date of opening/preparation. All ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods must be marked with the date of opening or preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41?F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.
